This month's featured designer, Cheryl Eisenmann, is an internationally recognized painter whose work is not pinned down to a particular style. Her summer paintings are reminiscent of a sunny day when the sky is a brilliant shade of blues and of spectacular contrast. She's best known for her courageous women as well as her American landscapes. At four different points in her life -- including the result of a lightning strike that gutted her nephew's home -- Eisenmann recovered her artistic ability.
Now living at her home in Scherds, Cheryl believes in being different. This week's art blog post featured a series of paintings that could be easily transported over a century-old freight elevator (possibly behind one of her residences) that was once used to move raw machine parts as they passed through the carports of factories all over town, allowing a neighbor from the street underneath to be women artists
